name: agent-builder-main-flow-decision
body:
Decision record for the `agent-builder-main-flow` change-set.

SOURCE. In-flight change-set blocked because the repo's code-writer agents are missing or outdated. Some LLMs wrongly refuse, reading the project-flow law "main is never a mutation place" as forbidding the agent-builder's `.opencode/agents/**` edits on main. The required process: navigator recognises the block → tasks the `agent-builder` subagent on the MAIN CHECKOUT → the agent-builder scaffolds/updates `.opencode/agents/**` and COMMITS on main → the navigator rebases the project worktree onto main → re-scans → the user restarts opencode and reconnects before implementation continues.

VERIFIED AGAINST THE BRANCH GRAPH. All three surfaces resolve as real `docs` File nodes: `opencode-suite/agents/agent-builder.md` (400 lines), `opencode-suite/agents/codebase-navigator.md` (569 lines), `AGENTS.md` (847 lines) — so `implemented-by` targets resolve and NO planned Implementation node is needed for them. `rust.apg.install`'s `AGENTS` table (`src/install.rs:255-277`) embeds `agent-builder.md` via `include_str!` into `~/.opencode/agents/`. Baseline confirmed in the files: `agent-builder.md`'s own frontmatter `bash:` block (lines 30-40) grants only the read-only git patterns, and rule 2 (line 259) says "You never build, run tests, or mutate git"; line 399 already states that opencode must be restarted for new agents/grants to load. `codebase-navigator.md` line 78 already grants the navigator `git rebase *`, and its "### Codebase agents (delegate — never scaffold or implement yourself)" section is at line 434. (The proposal's pointer to an AGENTS.md "Codebase agents" section around lines 744-770 is inaccurate — that area holds the plan/task/feedback and distributed-agent prose; the guide's relevant surfaces are its project-flow section and the agent-builder bullet at lines 758-770.)

MAIN-MUTATION CLARIFICATION. "Main is never a mutation place" is a statement about the binary's GUARDED mutations (durable `apg node`/`apg edge` and transient plan/review, which refuse outside a project worktree), not about agent definition. An agent is a consumer artifact loaded by the running opencode session from the main checkout; it must be committed there. This scoping is stated in the requirement, its `constraint`, and must land in the navigator/agent-builder templates and `AGENTS.md`.

SPEC AUTHORING. Added `requirements.requirement.agent-builder-main-flow` (feature `agent-builder-main-flow`) under the existing coordinator user `requirements.user.navigator-agent` (no agent-builder/spec-writer user exists — the tree models the coordinator actor, not each distributed subagent; the agent-builder is the delegated tool of the navigator, so a new user would duplicate that actor). Domain: `domain.entity.agent-scaffold-flow` (kind `entity`; bare, no group — it has no natural subdomain, mirroring the sibling `domain.entity.task-execution-cadence`). Solution: NEW `solution.component.agent-builder-prompt` (under `solution.container.opencode-suite`) plus reuse of `solution.component.codebase-navigator-prompt` and `solution.component.repo-agent-guide`. Spine: user ⊃ requirement —drives→ entity —realised-by→ the three components —implemented-by→ `opencode-suite/agents/agent-builder.md`, `opencode-suite/agents/codebase-navigator.md`, `AGENTS.md`. Added the law `requirements.constraint.agent-changes-always-on-main` (`attaches-to` the requirement).

SCOPE. This change-set edits three docs/product-source surfaces only. It does NOT edit `.opencode/agents/**` (consumer artifacts refreshed out-of-band with the installed release), adds NO tests, and makes NO binary change. [autonomous]
